content.content:
1	# Vision Dataset Workbench
2	
3	Vision Dataset Workbench is a local, CPU-friendly command-line foundation for organizing image datasets. It stores a small manifest beside the dataset, imports image metadata without uploading files, and reports basic dataset statistics.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	- Python 3.11 or newer
8	- No third-party runtime dependencies
9	
10	## Quick start
11	
12	```bash
13	python3 -m vision_workbench init ./workspace
14	python3 -m vision_workbench add ./workspace ./examples/cat.jpg --label cat
15	python3 -m vision_workbench summary ./workspace
16	```
17	
18	The manifest is written to `.vision-workbench/manifest.json`. Importing the same file twice is idempotent because records are keyed by the file content hash. Imports, batch writes, undos and plan creation are serialized by a single workspace lock and committed through the same write-ahead journal, so several local processes can operate on one workspace at once: every successful operation survives, concurrent imports of different content all land, and duplicate imports report `already present` once while keeping the first registration's source and label.
19	
20	A single-file `add` registers the file's full SHA-256 digest, byte size and
21	resolved absolute source path, and all three are read from the same stable
22	regular file: the source is checked before and after the read, and the read
23	itself is pinned to the confirmed file. If the source is rewritten, appended
24	to, truncated, deleted and recreated, or replaced by another file (even one
25	with identical content, size and modification time) while it is being
26	confirmed or read — or if the path vanishes, becomes a directory or a
27	symlink, or cannot be opened or read in full — the import fails with the
28	source path and the reason, and no sample is registered. Content that
29	happens to match an existing digest never masks such a failure. A source
30	path that is a symlink when the command starts is still followed and its
31	target imported.
32	
33	## Importing a directory
34	
35	A whole directory of images can be registered in one batch:
36	
37	```bash
38	python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --label cat
39	python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --recursive
40	```
41	
42	(The shorter `import` alias is equivalent.)
43	
44	- Only regular files with an extension of `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.bmp`,
45	  `.gif` or `.webp` (matched case-insensitively) are candidates. Symlinks
46	  and other entry types never qualify; recursion stays on the top level
47	  unless `--recursive` is given and never descends through symlinked
48	  directories. Files that appear after the scan are left for the next
49	  import.
50	- Candidates are ordered by their path relative to the source directory,
51	  with `/` separators, compared by Unicode code point.
52	- Samples are identified by their full SHA-256 digest. When several
53	  candidates share content that the workspace does not yet know, only the
54	  sorted-first candidate is added; the rest report `duplicate`. Digests
55	  already in the workspace always report `duplicate` and keep their
56	  original source, label and revision history — the batch label never
57	  overwrites an existing record.
58	- `--label` applies only to genuinely new samples. Omitting it leaves
59	  them unlabeled; the empty string also means unlabeled; any other string
60	  is kept literally.
61	- The result is JSON: the candidate count, the number added, the number
62	  of duplicates, and every candidate's relative path, full digest and
63	  `added`/`duplicate` status in scan order. Empty directories and
64	  all-duplicate imports succeed with zero added.
65	- The batch is all-or-nothing: a missing or non-directory source, a
66	  directory that cannot be scanned, a candidate that cannot be read in
67	  full, or a candidate whose identity, size or modification time changes
68	  while it is read fails the whole import with the path and reason and
69	  leaves no new samples. With `--recursive`, a subdirectory that was
70	  confirmed as a real directory and is then replaced by a symbolic link —
71	  wherever the link points — likewise fails the whole import with the
72	  subdirectory's path, rather than following the link or skipping the
73	  directory; the link target's images are neither imported nor reported
74	  as duplicates, and directories that were symlinks from the start are
75	  still simply ignored. The batch commits through the same journal as
76	  single-file imports, so an interruption shows either the old state or
77	  the complete batch, and concurrent label batches are never lost.
78	
79	## Split plans
80	
81	A split plan divides every sample currently in the manifest into a
82	train/validation/test set. Plans are saved under
83	`.vision-workbench/splits/<name>.json` and never change afterwards.
84	
85	```bash
86	python3 -m vision_workbench split create ./workspace baseline \
87	    --seed 42 --train 0.6 --validation 0.2 --test 0.2
88	python3 -m vision_workbench split show ./workspace baseline
89	```
90	
91	- The three ratios must be finite numbers in `[0, 1]` that sum to exactly
92	  one; any of them may be zero. Decimals (`0.1`) and fractions (`1/3`) are
93	  both accepted and handled with exact rational arithmetic.
94	- Stratification guarantees that, for every class and for the dataset as a
95	  whole, each set's count differs from its proportional expectation by
96	  strictly less than one — even for classes with one or two samples.
97	- Assignments depend only on sample content digests, labels and the seed,
98	  so they are stable across import order, manifest ordering, workspace
99	  location and restarts. Samples are listed by digest in each set.
100	- Unlabeled samples (no label or an empty label) form their own stratum,
101	  reported under the empty-string key `""`; a real class literally named
102	  `unlabeled` is kept separate.
103	- Creating under an existing name reuses the plan only when the seed,
104	  ratios, sample identities and labels all match; otherwise it reports a
105	  name conflict and leaves the original untouched. Sample identities and
106	  labels are snapshotted from one complete manifest state, so a batch that
107	  changes several labels is seen wholly before or wholly after the plan,
108	  never half-applied. Concurrent creation of one name is atomic: exactly
109	  one request creates it, identical requests reuse it and differing
110	  requests conflict; plans with different names all save, and a plan is
111	  only ever read whole or reported as not found.
112	
113	## Exporting a split plan
114	
115	A saved split plan can be exported as a portable, offline ZIP package:
116	
117	```bash
118	python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip
119	```
120	
121	- The package contains `train/`, `validation/` and `test/` directories,
122	  each with the same numbered ImageFolder class directories (`class_01`,
123	  `class_02`, ...), plus a UTF-8 `manifest.json`. Samples are stored as
124	  `<set>/<class>/<full-sha256><source-extension>`.
125	- The export uses only the saved plan: its samples, labels, set
126	  assignments and recorded source paths. Later imports, batch label
127	  changes or undos never alter an exported package, and exporting never
128	  writes to the workspace.
129	- All sets share one class directory numbering, even when a class has no
130	  samples in a set. Chinese labels, labels containing path separators and
131	  labels differing only in case each keep a distinct identity in the
132	  manifest's label-to-directory mapping; no machine-specific absolute
133	  paths are written.
134	- An empty plan exports the three set directories and an empty manifest.
135	- Samples with no label are unlabeled. By default the whole export is
136	  rejected and the offending digest is reported; `--skip-unlabeled` skips
137	  them instead, listing the per-set skip counts in both the result and the
138	  manifest. Skipping never redistributes other samples. A real class
139	  literally named `unlabeled` is exported normally.
140	- Source files are streamed and verified against the saved content digest
141	  while copying: a missing, non-regular, unreadable or changed source
142	  fails the whole export with the sample digest and reason.
143	- A single sample at or above 2 GiB (2,147,483,648 bytes of uncompressed
144	  content) is written as a ZIP64 entry automatically; large and ordinary
145	  samples may coexist in one plan and one package, and the large entry is
146	  still streamed in fixed chunks, so exporting it never needs memory for
147	  the whole file. This also covers multi-gigabyte content that compresses
148	  well: the decision follows the uncompressed size, so a tiny resulting
149	  package is not rejected. Plans containing only smaller samples keep
150	  exactly the classic archive format, byte for byte — ZIP64 fields appear
151	  only in the entries that require them. The manifest, the result counts
152	  and the set/class layout are identical either way, and packages remain
153	  extractable with standard ZIP64-aware tools.
154	- `--source-dir` reads sample files from a directory tree instead of the
155	  recorded source paths, which is useful after moving the dataset:
156	  ```bash
157	  python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip \
158	      --source-dir ./moved-dataset
159	  ```
160	  Every regular file under the directory and its subdirectories is
161	  considered (no extension filter, since files may have been renamed);
162	  symlinks and other non-regular entries are skipped and symlinked
163	  directories are never descended. Each exported sample must be matched
164	  to a file whose full SHA-256 matches the plan — a same-named file with
165	  different content does not qualify. When several files share content,
166	  the one whose `/`-separated relative path sorts first by Unicode code
167	  point is used. The selected copy is pinned to the actual read: the path
168	  is lstat()ed without following symlinks, opened without following a
169	  final symlink, and the opened descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be
170	  the exact regular file (same device and inode) captured during the
171	  lookup — the check covers the object that is really read, not just one
172	  look at the path before it opens. If the selected path is replaced
173	  after the lookup but before or while it is opened by another regular
174	  file — even one with identical content, size and modification time —
175	  or by a symlink, even one pointing at the original file, the whole
176	  export fails with the sample digest, the selected source path and the
177	  reason; no other same-content copy is substituted and the plan's
178	  recorded source path is not used as a fallback.
179	
180	  The directory walk is itself pinned to directory descriptors rather
181	  than path strings: each directory is entered with `openat`
182	  (`O_NOFOLLOW` and `O_DIRECTORY`) relative to its parent's descriptor
183	  and verified with `fstatat`, and the confirmed root stays open for the
184	  whole export. A subdirectory that is a real directory when the walk
185	  first reaches it but is replaced by a symlink before it is entered,
186	  while its contents are read, after the lookup or while the package is
187	  copied fails the whole export with the changed directory's path and
188	  the symlink reason — whether the link points outside the specified
189	  directory, inside it, or at the directory moved to its new location,
190	  and at any nesting level. The link's target is never read, matched or
191	  packaged, even if it holds a file byte-identical to the planned
192	  sample; no other normal copy and no still-readable recorded source are
193	  substituted. Before each matched file is copied its ancestor
194	  directories are re-verified the same way, and after all samples are
195	  streamed every directory from the walk is verified once more before
196	  the ZIP is published, so the target ZIP is never created and no
197	  incomplete export file remains. Only entries that are already
198	  symlinks the first time the walk meets them are skipped, as before.
199	
200	  Files unrelated to the
201	  plan are read (an unreadable file anywhere fails the export) but never
202	  included. The plan still decides
203	  sample identities, labels, set assignments and package file extensions;
204	  the lookup is used for this export only and is never written back. A
205	  missing or non-directory source, an unreadable directory or file, or a
206	  sample with no matching content fails the whole export with the path
207	  and reason; the package is byte-identical to a normal export of the
208	  same plan, options and content. For an empty plan (or when every sample
209	  is skipped) the directory only has to exist and be a directory.
210	- The target name is owned only once the whole package has been generated
211	  and fsynced and the source verification has passed, so a reader never
212	  sees a half-written file.  The name must be free both when the export
213	  starts and at the moment the finished package is published: another
214	  program that creates a file at the target path while the images are
215	  copied or compressed — even an empty file or one byte-identical to the
216	  package, and even in the last instant before publication — makes the
217	  export fail with the user-given target path as a name-already-taken
218	  conflict, a non-zero exit status and no result on standard output.
219	  That occupant is never overwritten, unlinked or moved, its content and
220	  file type are preserved, and this run's temporary package is removed.
221	  A symbolic link at the name counts as occupied too, including one that
222	  points at a location that does not exist; whether the link is there at
223	  the start or appears during the export, the link itself and its target
224	  are left in place and the ZIP is never written through it.  There is no
225	  overwrite option and no automatic alternative file name.  A failure or
226	  interruption otherwise leaves no incomplete file, and concurrent
227	  exports to the same path are serialized so at most one succeeds and the
228	  rest fail clearly with the same conflict.
229	- Package bytes are deterministic for a given plan, options and source
230	  content: exporting at a different time, from a copied workspace or to a
231	  different path yields byte-identical ZIPs, and source modification times
232	  do not matter.
233	
234	## Finding samples by label
235	
236	Samples can be listed by their current category label, so a class leads
237	straight to the full sample summaries needed for the label queries and
238	batch updates below — no need to page through the dataset listing.
239	
240	```bash
241	python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace cat     # a normal class
242	python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace 猫      # Chinese text, kept as-is
243	python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace ''      # unlabeled samples
244	python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace unlabeled  # the literal class
245	```
246	
247	The result is readable UTF-8 JSON: the queried label, the match count and
248	the sample list, each record giving the full SHA-256 digest, the source
249	path saved at first registration, the byte size and the current label.
250	Records are sorted ascending by full digest and `count` always equals the
251	list length. A digest is listed once no matter how many paths once
252	imported identical content, with the source from its first registration.
253	
254	- Matching is exact on the **current** registered label: case, leading or
255	  trailing whitespace and path separators are matched literally and are
256	  never trimmed, rewritten or interpreted as paths. Querying `cat` does
257	  not return `Cat` or `cat ` (cat followed by a space).
258	- The empty string queries **unlabeled** samples: records whose label is
259	  `null` or `""` both match, and every returned record shows its label as
260	  `null`. Querying the text `unlabeled` instead returns only samples
261	  whose real class is literally named `unlabeled`; it never includes
262	  unlabeled samples and does not use the summary statistics' display that
263	  merges the two.
264	- An empty workspace or a label with no matches is a normal result with
265	  `count` 0 and an empty list, not an error.
266	- The query reads only registered records. A successful batch update or
267	  undo is reflected by the next query; labels snapshotted in saved split
268	  plans neither match nor are changed, and a source image that has since
269	  moved, been deleted or become unreadable is still returned — the source
270	  file is never reopened and its recorded path is never updated.
271	
272	## Corrupted registrations
273	
274	Every command that uses the current manifest — `summary`, `label`,
275	`find-label`, `add`, `import-dir`, `batch`, `undo` and `split create` —
276	validates the **whole** `manifest.json` before using any sample, so a
277	damaged registration list can never surface as a runtime exception on one
278	record or make a label change touch only one of two duplicate records:
279	
280	- The manifest must be a JSON object whose `schema_version` is the integer
281	  `1` and whose `items` is a list. Booleans (`true`) and decimals (`1.0`)
282	  cannot stand in for the version.
283	- Each sample record must be an object with a full 64-character lowercase
284	  hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, a non-empty string source, a non-negative
285	  integer size, and a string or `null` label. Booleans, numeric strings and
286	  decimals are never accepted as sizes. One digest may be registered only
287	  once — even two otherwise identical records are an error, never merged.
288	- Valid records at the front of the list never mask a later bad record;
289	  the check covers the complete list, including records a query would not
290	  match.
291	
292	On any such problem the command exits with a non-zero status, prints
293	nothing on standard output and no traceback, and reports on standard error
294	that the **dataset manifest** is corrupted — naming the offending part, or
295	the record's 1-based position in the list together with the bad field (for
296	a duplicate digest, the digest and both positions). The operation is
297	refused outright: the existing manifest, the batch history and saved split
298	plans are never rewritten, pruned, default-filled or replaced by an empty
299	list. Manifests produced by older versions remain valid without migration —
300	records may lack the optional label revision and carry extra fields, both
301	of which are kept — and the empty list and zero-byte samples stay legal,
302	with `null` and `""` still meaning *unlabeled*.
303	
304	A source image that has since moved or been deleted is not corruption:
305	queries keep using the registered information. Features that depend only on
306	saved data also keep working regardless of the manifest: `history` reads
307	the batch history, and `split show` and `export` use the saved plan alone.
308	
309	## Tests
310	
311	```bash
312	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
313	```
314	
315	## Batch label updates
316	
317	Labels of already-imported samples can be changed in batches. A batch is a
318	UTF-8 JSON file:
319	
320	```json
321	{
322	  "batch": "renumber-2026-01",
323	  "changes": [
324	    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "cat", "new": "kitten"},
325	    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "dog", "new": null}
326	  ]
327	}
328	```
329	
330	- `batch` must be a non-empty string.
331	- `old` is the expected current label; `new` is the target label. Both may
332	  be a string or `null`; `null` and the empty string both mean *unlabeled*,
333	  any other string is taken literally (including Chinese text and a class
334	  named `unlabeled`).
335	- The whole batch is verified before anything is written: an unknown
336	  digest, a sample listed twice, a non-string/non-null label, a malformed
337	  file, or any sample whose current label differs from its expected old
338	  label rejects the entire batch with the offending record identified.
339	- Records whose target equals the current label are no-ops; if every
340	  record is a no-op, the batch reports `no-changes`, occupies no batch
341	  number and writes no history.
342	
343	```bash
344	python3 -m vision_workbench label ./workspace <digest>      # current label
345	python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace <label>  # samples of one label
346	python3 -m vision_workbench batch ./workspace changes.json   # submit a batch
347	python3 -m vision_workbench history ./workspace              # successful batches
348	python3 -m vision_workbench undo ./workspace <batch-number>  # undo a batch
349	```
350	
351	See [Finding samples by label](#finding-samples-by-label) for the
352	`find-label` query, including the empty-string query for unlabeled
353	samples.
354	
355	Submitting the same number with the same content again returns the
356	original result without re-modifying anything (list order and the
357	`null`/`""` spelling do not change the content), even if labels were
358	changed in the meantime. The same number with different content is a
359	conflict.
360	
361	`history` lists successful batches in submission order: the samples
362	involved, their before/after labels, and the number of samples actually
363	changed. Failed batches never enter history.
364	
365	`undo` restores the old labels of a batch, but only for samples the batch
366	actually changed and only when none of them was modified afterwards (even
367	if the label was changed back). Other samples' later changes do not block
368	the undo. Undo leaves a queryable record; repeating it reports
369	`already-undone`.
370	
371	### Corrupted batch history
372	
373	Every sample record stored for a successful batch carries a `rev`: the
374	sample's label revision at the moment the batch finished, which an undo
375	pins against. That `rev` is mandatory on **every** history record —
376	whether the record actually changed a label or not — and must be a genuine
377	non-negative integer. A boolean (`true`), a decimal (`1.0`), a numeric
378	string (`"1"`), `null` and a missing field are all invalid; a missing
379	revision is never treated as zero, and the integer `0` on an unchanged
380	record stays legal. This requirement is specific to batch history: the
381	optional `rev` on manifest registrations keeps its old compatibility
382	behaviour, including records that omit it.
383	
384	When an undo targets a batch containing such a record, the command exits
385	with a non-zero status, prints nothing on standard output and no
386	traceback, and reports on standard error that the **batch history** is
387	corrupted — naming the batch number, the sample's full SHA-256 digest and
388	the exact `rev` problem. The whole undo is refused even if an earlier

# Vision Dataset Workbench

Vision Dataset Workbench is a local, CPU-friendly command-line foundation for organizing image datasets. It stores a small manifest beside the dataset, imports image metadata without uploading files, and reports basic dataset statistics.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer
- No third-party runtime dependencies

## Quick start

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench init ./workspace
python3 -m vision_workbench add ./workspace ./examples/cat.jpg --label cat
python3 -m vision_workbench summary ./workspace
```

The manifest is written to `.vision-workbench/manifest.json`. Importing the same file twice is idempotent because records are keyed by the file content hash. Imports, batch writes, undos and plan creation are serialized by a single workspace lock and committed through the same write-ahead journal, so several local processes can operate on one workspace at once: every successful operation survives, concurrent imports of different content all land, and duplicate imports report `already present` once while keeping the first registration's source and label.

A single-file `add` registers the file's full SHA-256 digest, byte size and
resolved absolute source path, and all three are read from the same stable
regular file: the source is checked before and after the read, and the read
itself is pinned to the confirmed file. If the source is rewritten, appended
to, truncated, deleted and recreated, or replaced by another file (even one
with identical content, size and modification time) while it is being
confirmed or read — or if the path vanishes, becomes a directory or a
symlink, or cannot be opened or read in full — the import fails with the
source path and the reason, and no sample is registered. Content that
happens to match an existing digest never masks such a failure. A source
path that is a symlink when the command starts is still followed and its
target imported.

## Importing a directory

A whole directory of images can be registered in one batch:

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --label cat
python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --recursive
```

(The shorter `import` alias is equivalent.)

- Only regular files with an extension of `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.bmp`,
  `.gif` or `.webp` (matched case-insensitively) are candidates. Symlinks
  and other entry types never qualify; recursion stays on the top level
  unless `--recursive` is given and never descends through symlinked
  directories. Files that appear after the scan are left for the next
  import.
- Candidates are ordered by their path relative to the source directory,
  with `/` separators, compared by Unicode code point.
- Samples are identified by their full SHA-256 digest. When several
  candidates share content that the workspace does not yet know, only the
  sorted-first candidate is added; the rest report `duplicate`. Digests
  already in the workspace always report `duplicate` and keep their
  original source, label and revision history — the batch label never
  overwrites an existing record.
- `--label` applies only to genuinely new samples. Omitting it leaves
  them unlabeled; the empty string also means unlabeled; any other string
  is kept literally.
- The result is JSON: the candidate count, the number added, the number
  of duplicates, and every candidate's relative path, full digest and
  `added`/`duplicate` status in scan order. Empty directories and
  all-duplicate imports succeed with zero added.
- The batch is all-or-nothing: a missing or non-directory source, a
  directory that cannot be scanned, a candidate that cannot be read in
  full, or a candidate whose identity, size or modification time changes
  while it is read fails the whole import with the path and reason and
  leaves no new samples. With `--recursive`, a subdirectory that was
  confirmed as a real directory and is then replaced by a symbolic link —
  wherever the link points — likewise fails the whole import with the
  subdirectory's path, rather than following the link or skipping the
  directory; the link target's images are neither imported nor reported
  as duplicates, and directories that were symlinks from the start are
  still simply ignored. The batch commits through the same journal as
  single-file imports, so an interruption shows either the old state or
  the complete batch, and concurrent label batches are never lost.

## Split plans

A split plan divides every sample currently in the manifest into a
train/validation/test set. Plans are saved under
`.vision-workbench/splits/<name>.json` and never change afterwards.

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench split create ./workspace baseline \
    --seed 42 --train 0.6 --validation 0.2 --test 0.2
python3 -m vision_workbench split show ./workspace baseline
```

- The three ratios must be finite numbers in `[0, 1]` that sum to exactly
  one; any of them may be zero. Decimals (`0.1`) and fractions (`1/3`) are
  both accepted and handled with exact rational arithmetic.
- Stratification guarantees that, for every class and for the dataset as a
  whole, each set's count differs from its proportional expectation by
  strictly less than one — even for classes with one or two samples.
- Assignments depend only on sample content digests, labels and the seed,
  so they are stable across import order, manifest ordering, workspace
  location and restarts. Samples are listed by digest in each set.
- Unlabeled samples (no label or an empty label) form their own stratum,
  reported under the empty-string key `""`; a real class literally named
  `unlabeled` is kept separate.
- Creating under an existing name reuses the plan only when the seed,
  ratios, sample identities and labels all match; otherwise it reports a
  name conflict and leaves the original untouched. Sample identities and
  labels are snapshotted from one complete manifest state, so a batch that
  changes several labels is seen wholly before or wholly after the plan,
  never half-applied. Concurrent creation of one name is atomic: exactly
  one request creates it, identical requests reuse it and differing
  requests conflict; plans with different names all save, and a plan is
  only ever read whole or reported as not found.

## Exporting a split plan

A saved split plan can be exported as a portable, offline ZIP package:

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip
```

- The package contains `train/`, `validation/` and `test/` directories,
  each with the same numbered ImageFolder class directories (`class_01`,
  `class_02`, ...), plus a UTF-8 `manifest.json`. Samples are stored as
  `<set>/<class>/<full-sha256><source-extension>`.
- The export uses only the saved plan: its samples, labels, set
  assignments and recorded source paths. Later imports, batch label
  changes or undos never alter an exported package, and exporting never
  writes to the workspace.
- All sets share one class directory numbering, even when a class has no
  samples in a set. Chinese labels, labels containing path separators and
  labels differing only in case each keep a distinct identity in the
  manifest's label-to-directory mapping; no machine-specific absolute
  paths are written.
- An empty plan exports the three set directories and an empty manifest.
- Samples with no label are unlabeled. By default the whole export is
  rejected and the offending digest is reported; `--skip-unlabeled` skips
  them instead, listing the per-set skip counts in both the result and the
  manifest. Skipping never redistributes other samples. A real class
  literally named `unlabeled` is exported normally.
- Source files are streamed and verified against the saved content digest
  while copying: a missing, non-regular, unreadable or changed source
  fails the whole export with the sample digest and reason.
- A single sample at or above 2 GiB (2,147,483,648 bytes of uncompressed
  content) is written as a ZIP64 entry automatically; large and ordinary
  samples may coexist in one plan and one package, and the large entry is
  still streamed in fixed chunks, so exporting it never needs memory for
  the whole file. This also covers multi-gigabyte content that compresses
  well: the decision follows the uncompressed size, so a tiny resulting
  package is not rejected. Plans containing only smaller samples keep
  exactly the classic archive format, byte for byte — ZIP64 fields appear
  only in the entries that require them. The manifest, the result counts
  and the set/class layout are identical either way, and packages remain
  extractable with standard ZIP64-aware tools.
- `--source-dir` reads sample files from a directory tree instead of the
  recorded source paths, which is useful after moving the dataset:
  ```bash
  python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip \
      --source-dir ./moved-dataset
  ```
  Every regular file under the directory and its subdirectories is
  considered (no extension filter, since files may have been renamed);
  symlinks and other non-regular entries are skipped and symlinked
  directories are never descended. Each exported sample must be matched
  to a file whose full SHA-256 matches the plan — a same-named file with
  different content does not qualify. When several files share content,
  the one whose `/`-separated relative path sorts first by Unicode code
  point is used. The selected copy is pinned to the actual read: the path
  is lstat()ed without following symlinks, opened without following a
  final symlink, and the opened descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be
  the exact regular file (same device and inode) captured during the
  lookup — the check covers the object that is really read, not just one
  look at the path before it opens. If the selected path is replaced
  after the lookup but before or while it is opened by another regular
  file — even one with identical content, size and modification time —
  or by a symlink, even one pointing at the original file, the whole
  export fails with the sample digest, the selected source path and the
  reason; no other same-content copy is substituted and the plan's
  recorded source path is not used as a fallback.

  The directory walk is itself pinned to directory descriptors rather
  than path strings: each directory is entered with `openat`
  (`O_NOFOLLOW` and `O_DIRECTORY`) relative to its parent's descriptor
  and verified with `fstatat`, and the confirmed root stays open for the
  whole export. A subdirectory that is a real directory when the walk
  first reaches it but is replaced by a symlink before it is entered,
  while its contents are read, after the lookup or while the package is
  copied fails the whole export with the changed directory's path and
  the symlink reason — whether the link points outside the specified
  directory, inside it, or at the directory moved to its new location,
  and at any nesting level. The link's target is never read, matched or
  packaged, even if it holds a file byte-identical to the planned
  sample; no other normal copy and no still-readable recorded source are
  substituted. Before each matched file is copied its ancestor
  directories are re-verified the same way, and after all samples are
  streamed every directory from the walk is verified once more before
  the ZIP is published, so the target ZIP is never created and no
  incomplete export file remains. Only entries that are already
  symlinks the first time the walk meets them are skipped, as before.

  Files unrelated to the
  plan are read (an unreadable file anywhere fails the export) but never
  included. The plan still decides
  sample identities, labels, set assignments and package file extensions;
  the lookup is used for this export only and is never written back. A
  missing or non-directory source, an unreadable directory or file, or a
  sample with no matching content fails the whole export with the path
  and reason; the package is byte-identical to a normal export of the
  same plan, options and content. For an empty plan (or when every sample
  is skipped) the directory only has to exist and be a directory.
- The target name is owned only once the whole package has been generated
  and fsynced and the source verification has passed, so a reader never
  sees a half-written file.  The name must be free both when the export
  starts and at the moment the finished package is published: another
  program that creates a file at the target path while the images are
  copied or compressed — even an empty file or one byte-identical to the
  package, and even in the last instant before publication — makes the
  export fail with the user-given target path as a name-already-taken
  conflict, a non-zero exit status and no result on standard output.
  That occupant is never overwritten, unlinked or moved, its content and
  file type are preserved, and this run's temporary package is removed.
  A symbolic link at the name counts as occupied too, including one that
  points at a location that does not exist; whether the link is there at
  the start or appears during the export, the link itself and its target
  are left in place and the ZIP is never written through it.  There is no
  overwrite option and no automatic alternative file name.  A failure or
  interruption otherwise leaves no incomplete file, and concurrent
  exports to the same path are serialized so at most one succeeds and the
  rest fail clearly with the same conflict.
- Package bytes are deterministic for a given plan, options and source
  content: exporting at a different time, from a copied workspace or to a
  different path yields byte-identical ZIPs, and source modification times
  do not matter.

## Finding samples by label

Samples can be listed by their current category label, so a class leads
straight to the full sample summaries needed for the label queries and
batch updates below — no need to page through the dataset listing.

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace cat     # a normal class
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace 猫      # Chinese text, kept as-is
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace ''      # unlabeled samples
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace unlabeled  # the literal class
```

The result is readable UTF-8 JSON: the queried label, the match count and
the sample list, each record giving the full SHA-256 digest, the source
path saved at first registration, the byte size and the current label.
Records are sorted ascending by full digest and `count` always equals the
list length. A digest is listed once no matter how many paths once
imported identical content, with the source from its first registration.

- Matching is exact on the **current** registered label: case, leading or
  trailing whitespace and path separators are matched literally and are
  never trimmed, rewritten or interpreted as paths. Querying `cat` does
  not return `Cat` or `cat ` (cat followed by a space).
- The empty string queries **unlabeled** samples: records whose label is
  `null` or `""` both match, and every returned record shows its label as
  `null`. Querying the text `unlabeled` instead returns only samples
  whose real class is literally named `unlabeled`; it never includes
  unlabeled samples and does not use the summary statistics' display that
  merges the two.
- An empty workspace or a label with no matches is a normal result with
  `count` 0 and an empty list, not an error.
- The query reads only registered records. A successful batch update or
  undo is reflected by the next query; labels snapshotted in saved split
  plans neither match nor are changed, and a source image that has since
  moved, been deleted or become unreadable is still returned — the source
  file is never reopened and its recorded path is never updated.

## Corrupted registrations

Every command that uses the current manifest — `summary`, `label`,
`find-label`, `add`, `import-dir`, `batch`, `undo` and `split create` —
validates the **whole** `manifest.json` before using any sample, so a
damaged registration list can never surface as a runtime exception on one
record or make a label change touch only one of two duplicate records:

- The manifest must be a JSON object whose `schema_version` is the integer
  `1` and whose `items` is a list. Booleans (`true`) and decimals (`1.0`)
  cannot stand in for the version.
- Each sample record must be an object with a full 64-character lowercase
  hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, a non-empty string source, a non-negative
  integer size, and a string or `null` label. Booleans, numeric strings and
  decimals are never accepted as sizes. One digest may be registered only
  once — even two otherwise identical records are an error, never merged.
- Valid records at the front of the list never mask a later bad record;
  the check covers the complete list, including records a query would not
  match.

On any such problem the command exits with a non-zero status, prints
nothing on standard output and no traceback, and reports on standard error
that the **dataset manifest** is corrupted — naming the offending part, or
the record's 1-based position in the list together with the bad field (for
a duplicate digest, the digest and both positions). The operation is
refused outright: the existing manifest, the batch history and saved split
plans are never rewritten, pruned, default-filled or replaced by an empty
list. Manifests produced by older versions remain valid without migration —
records may lack the optional label revision and carry extra fields, both
of which are kept — and the empty list and zero-byte samples stay legal,
with `null` and `""` still meaning *unlabeled*.

A source image that has since moved or been deleted is not corruption:
queries keep using the registered information. Features that depend only on
saved data also keep working regardless of the manifest: `history` reads
the batch history, and `split show` and `export` use the saved plan alone.

## Tests

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

## Batch label updates

Labels of already-imported samples can be changed in batches. A batch is a
UTF-8 JSON file:

```json
{
  "batch": "renumber-2026-01",
  "changes": [
    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "cat", "new": "kitten"},
    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "dog", "new": null}
  ]
}
```

- `batch` must be a non-empty string.
- `old` is the expected current label; `new` is the target label. Both may
  be a string or `null`; `null` and the empty string both mean *unlabeled*,
  any other string is taken literally (including Chinese text and a class
  named `unlabeled`).
- The whole batch is verified before anything is written: an unknown
  digest, a sample listed twice, a non-string/non-null label, a malformed
  file, or any sample whose current label differs from its expected old
  label rejects the entire batch with the offending record identified.
- Records whose target equals the current label are no-ops; if every
  record is a no-op, the batch reports `no-changes`, occupies no batch
  number and writes no history.

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench label ./workspace <digest>      # current label
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace <label>  # samples of one label
python3 -m vision_workbench batch ./workspace changes.json   # submit a batch
python3 -m vision_workbench history ./workspace              # successful batches
python3 -m vision_workbench undo ./workspace <batch-number>  # undo a batch
```

See [Finding samples by label](#finding-samples-by-label) for the
`find-label` query, including the empty-string query for unlabeled
samples.

Submitting the same number with the same content again returns the
original result without re-modifying anything (list order and the
`null`/`""` spelling do not change the content), even if labels were
changed in the meantime. The same number with different content is a
conflict.

`history` lists successful batches in submission order: the samples
involved, their before/after labels, and the number of samples actually
changed. Failed batches never enter history.

`undo` restores the old labels of a batch, but only for samples the batch
actually changed and only when none of them was modified afterwards (even
if the label was changed back). Other samples' later changes do not block
the undo. Undo leaves a queryable record; repeating it reports
`already-undone`.

### Corrupted batch history

Every sample record stored for a successful batch carries a `rev`: the
sample's label revision at the moment the batch finished, which an undo
pins against. That `rev` is mandatory on **every** history record —
whether the record actually changed a label or not — and must be a genuine
non-negative integer. A boolean (`true`), a decimal (`1.0`), a numeric
string (`"1"`), `null` and a missing field are all invalid; a missing
revision is never treated as zero, and the integer `0` on an unchanged
record stays legal. This requirement is specific to batch history: the
optional `rev` on manifest registrations keeps its old compatibility
behaviour, including records that omit it.

When an undo targets a batch containing such a record, the command exits
with a non-zero status, prints nothing on standard output and no
traceback, and reports on standard error that the **batch history** is
corrupted — naming the batch number, the sample's full SHA-256 digest and
the exact `rev` problem. The whole undo is refused even if an earlier
record in the same batch was restorable: no sample changes label, and
neither the registration list nor the batch history is rewritten,
default-filled or given a new undo marker. This refusal is distinct from
the normal "sample modified after the batch" rejection and from an
unknown batch number — a corrupt record can never be reported as undone,
as having no changes, or as an unknown batch. Corruption is checked before
the repeated-undo short-circuit too, so a batch already marked undone
still surfaces its bad record instead of returning `already-undone`.
Damage in a different batch does not matter: only the target batch's
records are examined, so a valid batch still undoes normally.

Imports, batch writes and undos are crash-safe: a write-ahead journal
installs the manifest and the history together, so after an interruption
the workspace shows either the old state or the complete new state with
its history — labels and their history never straddle the two. Recovery
runs under the workspace lock at the start of every operation, so a
process that already has the workspace open also completes a peer's
prepared transaction without reopening; a sample imported successfully
afterwards is never rolled back by that recovery. Concurrent operations
are serialized by the lock, so no successful import or batch is lost and
two batches modifying the same sample from the same old label cannot both
win. Summary, label and history queries each observe one complete state
and never report corruption from an in-flight write. Saved split plans are
never touched by imports, label changes or undos; plans created afterwards
use the current labels, and the same-name reuse/conflict rules still
apply.

"""Confirm one ordinary regular file and open exactly that confirmed file.

This is the single file-confirmation rule shared by every entry point
that turns a path into sample bytes:

* single-file import (``DatasetStore.add``),
* whole-directory import (``DatasetStore.import_directory``), and
* ``--source-dir`` export, both when the source tree is looked up and
  when the selected copy is streamed into the package.

The rule:

1. The path is inspected *without following a final symlink*
   (``lstat`` / ``fstatat``); the object found there must be a regular
   file.  Callers that arrive through their own non-symlink walk
   (directory import, source-dir export) only ever confirm such paths,
   while single-file import resolves a symlink given as its argument
   before calling in here, so following links at the start stays an
   entry-point decision.
2. The path is opened with ``O_NOFOLLOW`` (relative to a pinned
   directory descriptor when the caller has one), so a symlink swapped
   onto the path after the inspection cannot redirect the open.
3. The opened descriptor is ``fstat()``ed and proved to be a regular
   file carrying the exact ``(device, inode)`` identity that was
   confirmed (or, for the export copy, the identity recorded during the
   lookup): a different regular file renamed onto the path — even one
   with identical content, size and modification time — is rejected
   just like a symlink, even one pointing at the original file.

What differs between entry points deliberately stays outside this
module:

* whether a path occupied by something else *after* a successful open
  still matters — import re-inspects the path once the read is done and
  requires the same file with the same size and mtime, while export
  keeps reading the already pinned descriptor (the path may be
  reoccupied without spoiling the confirmed bytes);
* the public exception type, wording and identifying information.

Failures are therefore reported as structured :class:`ConfirmationError`
reasons; each entry point translates them into its existing public
errors, preserving the path, digest and reason information callers rely
on.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import errno
import hashlib
import os
import stat
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
from typing import NamedTuple

# Samples are streamed in fixed chunks, so large files never need memory
# for their whole content; every reader below uses the same chunk size.
READ_CHUNK_SIZE = 1024 * 1024

# Open without following a final symlink; 0 on platforms lacking the flag.
_O_NOFOLLOW = getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)


class ConfirmStage(str, Enum):
    """Where in the confirm-then-open sequence a failure was detected."""

    INSPECT = "inspect"  # the no-follow lstat()/fstatat() before opening
    OPEN = "open"  # the O_NOFOLLOW open()
    PROVE = "prove"  # the fstat() of the freshly opened descriptor


class ConfirmReason(str, Enum):
    """What went wrong, independent of the caller's public wording."""

    ACCESS_ERROR = "access error"  # an underlying syscall failed; .error set
    NOT_REGULAR = "not a regular file"  # a non-symlink, non-regular object
    NOW_SYMLINK = "is now a symlink"  # the path became a final symlink
    WRONG_IDENTITY = "wrong identity"  # another object occupies the path


@dataclass
class ConfirmationError(Exception):
    """A path could not be confirmed as, or opened as, one stable file.

    ``status`` carries the inspection result when one was obtained, so a
    caller can tell symlinks from other non-regular objects; ``error``
    carries the underlying :class:`OSError` for access failures.
    """

    reason: ConfirmReason
    stage: ConfirmStage
    status: os.stat_result | None = None
    error: OSError | None = None

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debugging only
        return f"{self.reason.value} at {self.stage.value}"


def inspect_regular(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    dir_fd: int | None = None,
    expected: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
) -> os.stat_result:
    """Inspect ``path`` without following a final symlink and confirm it.

    Returns the status of the confirmed regular file.  When ``dir_fd``
    is given, ``path`` is interpreted relative to that descriptor
    (``fstatat``); otherwise it is ``lstat()``ed directly.

    ``expected`` optionally carries the ``(device, inode)`` the binding
    must still carry — the identity recorded during the source-dir
    lookup when the export copy re-confirms a selected path.  A path
    that is a symlink, is not a regular file, or no longer carries the
    expected identity raises :class:`ConfirmationError` before anything
    is opened.
    """
    try:
        if dir_fd is None:
            status = os.lstat(path)
        else:
            status = os.stat(path, dir_fd=dir_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
    except OSError as error:
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, error=error
        ) from error
    if stat.S_ISLNK(status.st_mode):
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.NOW_SYMLINK, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, status=status
        )
    if not stat.S_ISREG(status.st_mode):
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.NOT_REGULAR, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, status=status
        )
    if expected is not None and (status.st_dev, status.st_ino) != expected:
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.WRONG_IDENTITY, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, status=status
        )
    return status


def open_without_follow(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str], *, dir_fd: int | None = None
) -> int:
    """Open ``path`` read-only with ``O_NOFOLLOW``, never following a link.

    A final symlink swapped in after the inspection makes the open fail
    with ``ELOOP``, which is reported as :class:`ConfirmReason.NOW_SYMLINK`
    rather than a generic access error; every other open failure carries
    the original :class:`OSError`.  The descriptor belongs to the caller
    on success.
    """
    try:
        return os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | _O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=dir_fd)
    except OSError as error:
        reason = (
            ConfirmReason.NOW_SYMLINK
            if error.errno == errno.ELOOP
            else ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR
        )
        raise ConfirmationError(
            reason, ConfirmStage.OPEN, error=error
        ) from error


def prove_opened_regular(
    descriptor: int, confirmed: os.stat_result
) -> os.stat_result:
    """Prove ``descriptor`` is the confirmed regular file itself.

    The descriptor is ``fstat()``ed and must be a regular file carrying
    ``confirmed``'s ``(device, inode)``; this covers the object that is
    actually read, not just one look at the path before it was opened.
    On any rejection the descriptor is closed here, so no opened file is
    leaked by a failed confirmation.
    """
    try:
        opened = os.fstat(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        _close_quietly(descriptor)
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR, ConfirmStage.PROVE, error=error
        ) from error
    if not stat.S_ISREG(opened.st_mode) or (
        opened.st_dev,
        opened.st_ino,
    ) != (confirmed.st_dev, confirmed.st_ino):
        _close_quietly(descriptor)
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.WRONG_IDENTITY, ConfirmStage.PROVE, status=opened
        )
    return opened


class ConfirmedOpen(NamedTuple):
    """A successfully confirmed open.

    ``descriptor`` is the open read-only descriptor (owned by the
    caller), ``confirmed`` is the pre-open no-follow inspection the
    descriptor was proved against, and ``opened`` is the descriptor's
    own ``fstat()`` result — same object identity, but carrying the
    size used while streaming.
    """

    descriptor: int
    confirmed: os.stat_result
    opened: os.stat_result


def confirm_and_open_regular(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    dir_fd: int | None = None,
    expected: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
) -> ConfirmedOpen:
    """Inspect, open without following links, and prove the descriptor.

    Returns the open descriptor together with the pre-open inspection
    and the descriptor's own status.  The descriptor is owned by the
    caller; every failure path closes it.
    """
    confirmed_status = inspect_regular(path, dir_fd=dir_fd, expected=expected)
    descriptor = open_without_follow(path, dir_fd=dir_fd)
    opened = prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status)
    return ConfirmedOpen(descriptor, confirmed_status, opened)


def hash_descriptor(descriptor: int) -> str:
    """Stream ``descriptor`` in chunks and return its full SHA-256 digest.

    The descriptor is wrapped with ``fdopen`` and released by the
    wrapper whether the read succeeds or raises (and closed if the
    wrapping itself fails), so a caller never has to reclaim it.
    """
    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
    try:
        stream = os.fdopen(descriptor, "rb")
    except BaseException:
        _close_quietly(descriptor)
        raise
    with stream:
        while True:
            chunk = stream.read(READ_CHUNK_SIZE)
            if not chunk:
                break
            hasher.update(chunk)
    return hasher.hexdigest()


def same_identity(left: os.stat_result, right: os.stat_result) -> bool:
    """Whether two stat results name the same object (device and inode)."""
    return (left.st_dev, left.st_ino) == (right.st_dev, right.st_ino)


def same_identity_size_mtime(
    left: os.stat_result, right: os.stat_result
) -> bool:
    """Whether both results describe the same unchanged file.

    Beyond the object identity this compares the byte size and
    modification time (nanosecond precision), which import requires
    before and after a read so in-place rewrites, appends and truncation
    are rejected as well as replacements.
    """
    return (
        left.st_dev,
        left.st_ino,
        left.st_size,
        left.st_mtime_ns,
    ) == (
        right.st_dev,
        right.st_ino,
        right.st_size,
        right.st_mtime_ns,
    )


def _close_quietly(descriptor: int) -> None:
    try:
        os.close(descriptor)
    except OSError:
        pass

1	"""Portable offline export of a saved split plan.
2	
3	An export package is a self-contained ZIP: one directory per set
4	(``train``/``validation``/``test``), each containing the same numbered
5	ImageFolder class directories, plus a UTF-8 JSON manifest.  Samples are
6	stored under ``<set>/<class>/<full-sha256><source-extension>``.
7	
8	The export is driven solely by the saved plan: its sample identities,
9	labels, set assignments and recorded source paths.  Later imports, label
10	changes or undos never affect an exported package, and exporting never
11	writes to the workspace.
12	
13	When ``source_dir`` is given, files are read from that directory tree
14	instead of the recorded source paths: every regular file under the
15	directory (no extension filter; symlinks and other non-regular entries
16	are skipped and symlinked directories are never descended) is read in
17	full and identified by content digest, and each exported sample is
18	matched to a file whose full SHA-256 matches the plan.  The selected
19	copy is pinned through the open (lstat without symlink follow,
20	``O_NOFOLLOW`` and an fstat of the descriptor), so the bytes read come
21	from the exact regular file confirmed at lookup time; a replacement
22	landing after the lookup — another regular file, even with identical
23	content, or a symlink, even pointing at the original file — fails the
24	export.
25	
26	The walk itself is anchored to directory descriptors: the confirmed
27	root is held open for the whole export and each directory is entered
28	with ``openat`` (``O_NOFOLLOW`` plus ``O_DIRECTORY``) relative to its
29	parent's descriptor and verified with ``fstatat`` on both the
30	parent-relative name and the opened descriptor, so a real subdirectory
31	cannot be followed through even if its path is swapped for a symlink in
32	the gap between its first inspection and its entry.  A subdirectory
33	confirmed real during the walk that is a symlink by the time it is
34	entered — whether the link points outside the tree, inside it, or at
35	the moved original — fails the whole export naming that path and the
36	symlink; the same applies to a swap landing while its children are
37	being processed.
38	
39	The protection extends to the package copy that follows the lookup.
40	Before each matched file is opened its ancestor directories are
41	re-derived and re-pinned through the same descriptor-anchored checks,
42	and after every sample has been streamed every directory recorded
43	during the walk is verified once more before the package is published:
44	a real directory replaced by a symlink after the lookup — before a
45	sample is opened, while a sample is read or between samples — still
46	fails the export, and a byte-equal file behind the new link is never
47	read, matched or packaged.  Entries that are symlinks when first
48	encountered keep being skipped exactly as before.
49	
50	The new directory only changes where bytes are read from; sample
51	identities, labels, set assignments and package file extensions remain
52	the plan's.  The lookup is used for this one export only and is never
53	written back.
54	
55	ZIP bytes are deterministic for a given plan, options and source content:
56	entry metadata uses fixed values, entries are written in a fixed order and
57	source modification times are never consulted.
58	
59	A single sample whose bytes reach the classic ZIP 32-bit size limit
60	(2 GiB, or close enough that its deflated form could) is written as a
61	ZIP64 entry: the local file header carries a ZIP64 extra field with the
62	real sizes while the entry is streamed, so no sample has to fit in
63	memory and highly compressible multi-gigabyte content is supported even
64	when the resulting package stays small.  Plans containing only smaller
65	samples use exactly the classic format they always did, byte for byte.
66	"""

105	def _entry_needs_zip64(file_size: int) -> bool:
106	    """Whether one sample entry must use the ZIP64 local header.
107	
108	    Mirrors zipfile's own pre-streaming heuristic (the uncompressed size
109	    plus a 5% margin, compared with the 32-bit size field limit): the
110	    margin covers both a size landing at the exact limit and deflate
111	    growth past it on incompressible content, while everything below it
112	    keeps the classic header byte for byte.
113	    """
114	    return file_size * 21 > zipfile.ZIP64_LIMIT * 20

117	def export_split(
118	    store: Any,
119	    plan_name: str,
120	    target: Path,
121	    skip_unlabeled: bool = False,
122	    source_dir: Path | None = None,
123	) -> dict[str, Any]:
124	    """Export a saved split plan to a new ZIP at ``target``.
125	
126	    Returns a result payload describing the plan, the number of samples
127	    actually exported, the class distribution per set and the per-set skip
128	    counts.  Raises :class:`ExportError` (a ``ValueError``) on any failure;
129	    the target path is never created in that case.
130	
131	    When ``source_dir`` is given, sample bytes are read from that directory
132	    tree instead of the plan's recorded source paths: the directory is
133	    walked (regular files only, no extension filter, never through
134	    symlinks), every regular file is hashed in full, and each exported
135	    sample is matched to a file with the same full SHA-256 digest.  The
136	    plan still decides identities, labels, set assignments and package
137	    file extensions; the lookup is used for this export only.
138	
139	    The walk is anchored to directory descriptors, so a subdirectory that
140	    was a real directory when the walk reached it but has become a symlink
141	    before it is entered or while its contents are read fails the export
142	    naming that path; the link is never followed.
143	    """
144	    plan = store.get_split(plan_name)
145	    members = _collect_members(plan)
146	
147	    unlabeled = [member for member in members if member["label"] == ""]
148	    if unlabeled and not skip_unlabeled:
149	        first = min(unlabeled, key=lambda member: member["sha256"])
150	        raise ExportError(
151	            f"sample {first['sha256']} in set {first['set']} has no label; "
152	            "pass --skip-unlabeled to export without unlabeled samples"
153	        )
154	
155	    exported = [member for member in members if member["label"] != ""]
156	    skipped_counts = {set_name: 0 for set_name in SET_NAMES}
157	    for member in unlabeled:
158	        skipped_counts[member["set"]] += 1
159	
160	    classes = _build_classes(exported)
161	    manifest = _build_manifest(plan, classes, exported, skipped_counts)
162	    distributions = _distributions(exported)
163	
164	    resolver = None
165	    if source_dir is not None:
166	        source_dir = Path(source_dir)
167	        if not source_dir.exists():
168	            raise ExportError(f"source directory does not exist: {source_dir}")
169	        if not source_dir.is_dir():
170	            raise ExportError(f"source is not a directory: {source_dir}")
171	        # An empty plan (or every sample skipped) needs no files at all;
172	        # the directory still has to exist and be one.
173	        if exported:
174	            resolved_root = source_dir.resolve()
175	            # Keep the confirmed root open and pinned for the whole
176	            # export: the lookup and the later package copy both resolve
177	            # through this descriptor, so a subdirectory turned into a
178	            # symlink after the lookup cannot be traversed while reading
179	            # the package bytes either.
180	            try:
181	                root_fd = os.open(resolved_root, os.O_RDONLY | _O_DIRECTORY)
182	            except OSError as error:
183	                raise ExportError(
184	                    f"cannot scan directory {resolved_root}: {error}"
185	                ) from error
186	            try:
187	                resolver = _scan_source_directory(resolved_root)
188	                for member in exported:
189	                    if member["sha256"] not in resolver:
190	                        raise ExportError(
191	                            f"sample {member['sha256']} in set {member['set']}: "
192	                            f"no file with matching content (full SHA-256 "
193	                            f"{member['sha256']}) found under source directory "
194	                            f"{source_dir}"
195	                        )
196	                directory_ids = getattr(resolver, "directory_ids", None)
197	                anchor = (
198	                    _SourceAnchor(root_fd, resolved_root, directory_ids)
199	                    if directory_ids is not None
200	                    else None
201	                )
202	                _write_package(
203	                    target,
204	                    classes,
205	                    exported,
206	                    manifest,
207	                    resolver,
208	                    source_anchor=anchor,
209	                )
210	            finally:
211	                os.close(root_fd)
212	        else:
213	            _write_package(target, classes, exported, manifest, None)
214	    else:
215	        _write_package(target, classes, exported, manifest, None)
216	
217	    return {
218	        "plan": plan["name"],
219	        "exported": len(exported),
220	        "skipped": skipped_counts,
221	        "sets": {
222	            set_name: {
223	                "samples": distributions[set_name]["samples"],
224	                "distribution": dict(
225	                    sorted(distributions[set_name]["distribution"].items())
226	                ),
227	            }
228	            for set_name in SET_NAMES
229	        },
230	        "target": str(target.resolve()),
231	    }

234	def _collect_members(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
235	    """Flatten plan members and validate the fields export depends on."""
236	    members: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
237	    for set_name in SET_NAMES:
238	        payload = plan["sets"][set_name]
239	        for member in payload["members"]:
240	            digest = member.get("sha256")
241	            label = member.get("label")
242	            source = member.get("source")
243	            if not isinstance(digest, str) or not _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(digest):
244	                raise ExportError(
245	                    f"split plan {plan.get('name')!r} is corrupted: "
246	                    f"sample {digest!r} is not a full SHA-256 digest"
247	                )
248	            if not isinstance(label, str):
249	                raise ExportError(
250	                    f"split plan {plan.get('name')!r} is corrupted: "
251	                    f"sample {digest} has a non-string label"
252	                )
253	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
254	                raise ExportError(
255	                    f"split plan {plan.get('name')!r} is corrupted: "
256	                    f"sample {digest} has no recorded source path"
257	                )
258	            members.append(
259	                {
260	                    "sha256": digest,
261	                    "label": label,
262	                    "source": source,
263	                    "set": set_name,
264	                }
265	            )
266	    return members

269	def _build_classes(members: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, str]:
270	    """Map every exported label to one shared numbered class directory.
271	
272	    All sets use the same numbering; labels are sorted by their literal
273	    text so Chinese labels, labels containing path separators and labels
274	    differing only in case each get a distinct, collision-free directory.
275	    """
276	    labels = sorted({member["label"] for member in members})
277	    width = max(2, len(str(len(labels)))) if labels else 2
278	    return {label: f"class_{index:0{width}d}" for index, label in enumerate(labels, 1)}

281	def _build_manifest(
282	    plan: dict[str, Any],
283	    classes: dict[str, str],
284	    members: list[dict[str, Any]],
285	    skipped_counts: dict[str, int],
286	) -> dict[str, Any]:
287	    set_summaries = {}
288	    for set_name in SET_NAMES:
289	        set_members = [member for member in members if member["set"] == set_name]
290	        set_summaries[set_name] = {
291	            "samples": len(set_members),
292	            "skipped": skipped_counts[set_name],
293	        }
294	
295	    sample_entries = []
296	    for member in sorted(members, key=lambda item: item["sha256"]):
297	        arc_path = _sample_path(member, classes[member["label"]])
298	        sample_entries.append(
299	            {
300	                "sha256": member["sha256"],
301	                "label": member["label"],
302	                "set": member["set"],
303	                "path": arc_path,
304	            }
305	        )
306	
307	    return {
308	        "schema_version": EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION,
309	        "plan": plan["name"],
310	        "seed": plan["seed"],
311	        "ratios": {set_name: plan["ratios"][set_name] for set_name in SET_NAMES},
312	        "classes": [
313	            {"label": label, "directory": directory}
314	            for label, directory in sorted(classes.items())
315	        ],
316	        "sets": set_summaries,
317	        "samples": sample_entries,
318	    }

322	    """Package-relative path for a sample: ``<set>/<class>/<digest><ext>``."""

327	def _distributions(members: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
328	    result: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
329	    for set_name in SET_NAMES:

338	# A resolver maps a full SHA-256 digest to the absolute path of the
339	# sorted-first regular file carrying that content, plus the file's
340	# identity (device, inode) captured during the lookup.  The copy opens
341	# that exact inode pinned through the open, so a swap after the lookup —
342	# another regular file, even with identical content, or a symlink, even
343	# one pointing at the original file — cannot be read in its place.
344	Resolver = dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]]

347	class _ScanResult(dict):
348	    """The digest resolver, also carrying every real directory seen.
349	
350	    Behaves as the plain digest-to-file resolver mapping, with an extra
351	    ``directory_ids`` attribute: each key is a ``/``-separated path
352	    relative to the root (``""`` for the root itself) and each value is
353	    ``(display path, device, inode)`` as observed during the walk.
354	    """
355	
356	    def __init__(
357	        self,
358	        files: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
359	        directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
360	    ) -> None:
361	        super().__init__(files)
362	        self.directory_ids = directories
363	
364	
365	def _scan_source_directory(root: Path) -> Resolver:
366	    """Walk ``root`` and map every digest to the sorted-first copy.
367	
368	    The directory and all its subdirectories are searched for regular
369	    files only: there is no extension filter, symlinks and other
370	    non-regular entries are skipped, and recursion never descends through
371	    symlinked directories.  Every regular file found is read in full and
372	    identified by its content digest; when several files share content,
373	    the one whose slash-separated path relative to ``root`` sorts first
374	    by Unicode code point owns the digest.  A directory that cannot be
375	    scanned, an entry that cannot be inspected or a file that cannot be
376	    read in full fails the export with the path and reason.
377	
378	    Every step is anchored to directory descriptors rather than path
379	    strings: a child is typed and entered with ``fstatat``/``openat``
380	    relative to the descriptor of the directory it was listed from, and
381	    each entered directory is pinned for the whole time its contents are
382	    processed.  A real subdirectory whose path is swapped for a symlink
383	    after it was listed but before or while it is entered therefore can
384	    never be followed — the open refuses the link and the export fails
385	    naming that directory — and a swap landing while its children are
386	    being read is detected when its path binding is re-checked after the
387	    children have been processed.  Only entries that are already
388	    symlinks when first listed are skipped, preserving the original
389	    convention.
390	    """
391	    try:
392	        root_fd = os.open(root, os.O_RDONLY | _O_DIRECTORY)
393	    except OSError as error:
394	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
395	    try:
396	        return _scan_tree(root_fd, root)
397	    finally:
398	        os.close(root_fd)
399	
400	
401	def _scan_tree(root_fd: int, root: Path) -> _ScanResult:
402	    """Walk the tree reached through the already-open, pinned ``root_fd``."""
403	    found: dict[str, tuple[str, Path, int, int]] = {}
404	    directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]] = {}
405	    try:
406	        root_status = os.fstat(root_fd)
407	    except OSError as error:
408	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
409	    directories[""] = (root, root_status.st_dev, root_status.st_ino)
410	    _walk_directory(root_fd, None, root, root, found, directories)
411	    files = {
412	        digest: (path, device, inode)
413	        for digest, (_, path, device, inode) in found.items()
414	    }
415	    return _ScanResult(files, directories)

418	def _walk_directory(
419	    parent_fd: int,
420	    name: str | None,
421	    display: Path,
422	    root: Path,
423	    found: dict[str, tuple[str, Path, int, int]],
424	    directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
425	) -> None:
426	    """Process one directory, anchored to a pinned descriptor.
427	
428	    ``name`` is the parent-relative basename; ``None`` marks the already
429	    open ``root`` whose descriptor is ``parent_fd``.  Any other
430	    directory is entered through :func:`_enter_subdirectory`, which
431	    pins the exact directory listed by the parent.
432	    """
433	    if name is None:
434	        directory_fd = parent_fd
435	        entered = False
436	    else:
437	        directory_fd = _enter_subdirectory(parent_fd, name, display)
438	        entered = True
439	    try:
440	        if entered:
441	            try:
442	                pinned = os.fstat(directory_fd)
443	            except OSError as error:
444	                raise ExportError(
445	                    f"cannot scan directory {display}: {error}"
446	                ) from error
447	            rel = os.path.relpath(display, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
448	            directories[rel] = (display, pinned.st_dev, pinned.st_ino)
449	        try:
450	            entries = list(os.scandir(directory_fd))
451	        except OSError as error:
452	            raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {display}: {error}") from error
453	        for entry in entries:
454	            child_name = entry.name
455	            child_display = display / child_name
456	            try:
457	                status = os.stat(
458	                    child_name, dir_fd=directory_fd, follow_symlinks=False
459	                )
460	            except OSError as error:
461	                raise ExportError(
462	                    f"cannot inspect entry {child_display}: {error}"
463	                ) from error
464	            mode = status.st_mode
465	            if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
466	                # A symlink when first encountered: skipped, never read.
467	                continue
468	            if stat.S_ISREG(mode):
469	                digest, device, inode = _hash_regular_file_at(
470	                    directory_fd, child_name, child_display
471	                )
472	                rel = os.path.relpath(child_display, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
473	                current = found.get(digest)
474	                if current is None or rel < current[0]:
475	                    found[digest] = (rel, child_display, device, inode)
476	            elif stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
477	                _walk_directory(
478	                    directory_fd,
479	                    child_name,
480	                    child_display,
481	                    root,
482	                    found,
483	                    directories,
484	                )
485	            # Any other entry type is skipped as before.
486	        if entered:
487	            # The children are done and were all reached through this
488	            # pinned descriptor.  Re-prove the parent-relative name still
489	            # binds to this same directory: a symlink (or anything else)
490	            # swapped onto it while the children were being processed
491	            # must fail the export even though nothing was read through
492	            # that link.
493	            _assert_still_same_directory(
494	                parent_fd, name, display, directory_fd
495	            )
496	    finally:
497	        if entered:
498	            os.close(directory_fd)
499
